0: How many surahs are there in the Quran?
They are arranged roughly from the longest to the shortest, not in the order of revelation.
1: What is the first surah of the Quran, in the order of the mushaf?
“The Opening”: it is recited in every rak‘a of the prayer. It is also called “Umm al-Kitab”, the Mother of the Book.
2: What is the longest surah of the Quran?
3: In which language was the Quran revealed?
The Quran says so itself: “We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran” (12:2).
4: Which angel brought the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ?
The Quran also calls him “the Trustworthy Spirit” (ar-Ruh al-Amin, 26:193).
5: In which cave did the first revelation take place?
The cave of Thawr is where the Prophet ﷺ hid with Abu Bakr during the Hijra.
6: What is the first word of the Quran that was revealed?
7: What is the last surah of the Quran, in the order of the mushaf?
Together with Al-Falaq, these are the two surahs of protection (al-mu‘awwidhatan) the Prophet ﷺ recited before sleeping (Bukhari).
8: In which month did the revelation of the Quran begin?
“The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was sent down” (2:185).
9: What is the shortest surah of the Quran?
10: Which surah is named after a woman?
Surah 19. Maryam is the only woman named in the Quran, more than 30 times.
11: What do we call a person who has memorised the whole Quran?
The word comes from “hafiza”, to guard, to preserve. Millions of Muslims, many of them children, know the Quran by heart.
12: Which is the only surah that does not begin with “Bismillah”?
Surah 9. One explanation attributed to ‘Ali: it opens with the ending of a pact, which does not fit the formula of mercy.
13: Over roughly how many years was the Quran revealed?
13 years in Mecca, then 10 years in Medina, from 610 to 632.
14: What is the name of the night when the revelation of the Quran began?
“Better than a thousand months” (97:3). It is sought in the odd nights of the last ten days of Ramadan.
15: According to a hadith, which surah is equal to a third of the Quran?
Reported by al-Bukhari. In four verses it sums up the oneness of Allah (tawhid).
16: Which verse is considered the greatest verse of the Quran?
Ayat al-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne)
17: Under which caliph was the Quran first compiled into a single volume?
Under ‘Uthman, official copies were later sent to the provinces.
18: Under which caliph were official copies of the Quran sent to the main cities?
He had these copies made from Abu Bakr's compilation, kept by Hafsa, to unify the reading across the whole empire.
19: Which companion was given the task of compiling the Quran?
A young scribe of the revelation, he knew the Quran by heart. He said that moving a mountain would have been easier for him (Bukhari).
20: Into how many parts (juz') is the Quran divided?
This division makes it possible to read the whole Quran in a month, one juz' a day, for example during Ramadan.
21: What does “An-Nahl”, the name of Surah 16, mean?
Verse 69 mentions the honey that comes from their bellies, “a healing for people”.
22: What does “Al-‘Ankabut”, the name of Surah 29, mean?
Verse 41 compares those who take protectors other than Allah to the spider: its house is the frailest of houses.
23: Which surah tells the story of the young men of the cave?
Surah 18. According to a hadith, reading it on Friday is a light for the believer (Hakim). It also tells the story of Musa and al-Khidr.
24: Which surah tells a prophet's whole story, called “the most beautiful of stories”?
“We relate to you the most beautiful of stories” (12:3). It is the only surah that tells a prophet's whole life from beginning to end.
25: What are the surahs revealed before the Hijra called?
They speak mainly about faith: the oneness of Allah, the Last Day, the prophets. The Medinan surahs deal more with laws and community life.
26: In which surah does the refrain “Which then of the favours of your Lord will you deny?” recur?
This refrain occurs 31 times in the surah.
27: Which surah contains the longest verse of the Quran?
28: Which prophet is mentioned by name most often in the Quran?
He is mentioned about 136 times. His story with Pharaoh comes up in many surahs.
29: How many times does the name “Muhammad” appear in the Quran?
He is also called “Ahmad” once, in Surah As-Saff.
30: In which surah is the Prophet ﷺ called “Ahmad”?
Verse 6: ‘Isa announces a messenger after him “whose name will be Ahmad”.
31: Who is the only companion of the Prophet ﷺ named in the Quran?
32: Which surah contains the formula “Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim” twice?
At the beginning and in verse 30, in Sulayman's letter.
33: How many surahs begin with isolated letters (like “Alif Lam Mim”)?
Like Al-Baqara (Alif Lam Mim) or Ya-Sin. For many scholars, their exact meaning is known only to Allah.
34: In which city was the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born?
Around the year 570, in the clan of Banu Hashim, of the tribe of Quraysh.
35: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ mother?
She died when he was 6, at al-Abwa', on the road to Medina.
36: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ father?
He died before the Prophet ﷺ was born, so the Prophet was born without a father.
37: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ first wife?
A wealthy merchant, she was the first to believe in him. As long as she lived, he married no other woman.
38: At what age did the Prophet ﷺ receive the first revelation?
In the cave of Hira', in 610, when Jibril said to him: “Read!”
39: To which city did the Prophet ﷺ emigrate during the Hijra?
In 622. The city was called Yathrib; it became “the City of the Prophet” (Madinat an-Nabi).
40: Which uncle raised and protected the Prophet ﷺ?
He protected him all his life against Quraysh, without ever embracing Islam.
41: At what age did the Prophet ﷺ pass away?
In the year 11 AH (632), in Medina, in ‘A'isha's room.
42: Which companion accompanied the Prophet ﷺ during the Hijra?
‘Ali stayed behind in Mecca, in the Prophet's ﷺ bed, to deceive his enemies.
43: What nickname, meaning “the trustworthy”, did the Prophet ﷺ have before prophethood?
Even his enemies entrusted their belongings to him. During the Hijra, he asked ‘Ali to return them to their owners.
44: Which wet nurse nursed the Prophet ﷺ in the desert?
He spent his first years with her, in the desert of Banu Sa‘d, where the air and the Arabic language were purer.
45: Which daughter of the Prophet ﷺ married ‘Ali?
Mother of al-Hasan and al-Husayn. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Fatima is a part of me” (Bukhari).
46: To which tribe did the Prophet ﷺ belong?
The tribe that guarded the Ka‘ba. A surah bears its name (Surah 106).
47: What is the year of the Prophet's ﷺ birth called?
The year Abraha tried to destroy the Ka‘ba with an army of elephants, driven back by birds (Surah 105).
48: What was the first major battle of the Muslims?
In the year 2 AH, during Ramadan: about 313 Muslims against nearly 1,000 Meccans.
49: In which battle did the Muslims dig a trench around Medina?
In the year 5 AH: a coalition of about 10,000 men besieged Medina without managing to cross the trench.
50: Which companion suggested digging the trench around Medina?
It was a Persian technique, unknown to the Arabs. The Prophet ﷺ dug himself alongside his companions.
51: What is the Prophet's ﷺ night journey from Mecca to Jerusalem called?
It is followed by the ascension to the heavens, al-Mi‘raj.
52: Which treaty was made with Quraysh in the year 6 AH?
It seemed unfavourable to the Muslims, but the Quran calls it “a clear victory” (48:1). It paved the way for the conquest of Mecca.
53: In which year of the Hijra was Mecca conquered?
The Prophet ﷺ entered almost without fighting, forgave most of his former enemies and had the idols of the Ka‘ba destroyed.
54: Which uncle of the Prophet ﷺ is called “the Lion of Allah”?
He died as a martyr at Uhud. The Prophet ﷺ called him “the master of martyrs” (Hakim).
55: Where is the Prophet ﷺ buried?
Prophets are buried where they die. This room was later included in the extension of the mosque.
56: In which country did Muslims find refuge before the Hijra?
There they were protected by the Christian king, an-Najashi (the Negus).
57: What was the first mosque built by the Prophet ﷺ?
Built on his arrival in Medina. According to the hadith, praying there equals an ‘umra (Tirmidhi, Ibn Maja).
58: What is the year in which the Prophet ﷺ lost Khadija and Abu Talib called?
Around 619, three years before the Hijra.
59: In which city was the Prophet ﷺ rejected and driven out with stones?
Wounded, he still refused that they be punished, hoping their descendants would worship Allah (Bukhari, Muslim). Taif embraced Islam later.
60: What is the name of the Prophet's ﷺ last pilgrimage, where he gave a famous sermon?
In the year 10 AH. At ‘Arafa he recalled the sanctity of life and property, and the equality of people.
61: At what age did the Prophet ﷺ lose his mother?
His mother Amina died at al-Abwa', on the way back from a visit to Medina.
62: Which grandfather took care of the Prophet ﷺ after his mother's death?
He died two years later; his uncle Abu Talib then took over.
63: Roughly how many Muslims fought at Badr?
The same number as the soldiers of Talut who crossed the river with him, according to a companion (Bukhari).
64: What was the name of the son of the Prophet ﷺ and Mariya, who died as a baby?
He died at about 18 months. An eclipse happened that day; the Prophet ﷺ explained it had nothing to do with anyone's death (Bukhari).
65: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ she-camel during the Hijra?
Al-Buraq is the mount of the night journey.
66: What is the pledge of allegiance of the people of Medina, made near Mecca before the Hijra, called?
Two pledges, in 621 and 622, near Mina. They prepared the emigration to Medina.
67: Which companion was the first free adult man to embrace Islam?
Khadija was the first person to believe, and ‘Ali the first child.
68: Who is the first man and the first prophet?
Allah taught him the names of all things (2:31) and commanded the angels to prostrate before him.
69: Only the believers and pairs of animals were saved from the flood. His own son refused to board.
70: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish?
In the belly of the fish he prayed: “La ilaha illa anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu mina z-zalimin” (21:87).
71: Which prophet built the Ka‘ba with his son Isma‘il?
While building, they prayed: “Our Lord, accept this from us” (2:127).
72: To which prophet was the Torah revealed?
It was given to him on tablets, after his meeting with Allah at Mount Sinai.
73: Which prophet was born without a father?
Adam, for his part, was created without father or mother.
74: Which prophet was thrown into a well by his brothers?
Jealous of their father's love for him, his brothers threw him into a well. He later became a minister in Egypt.
75: Which prophet understood the language of animals and commanded the jinn?
He even understood an ant warning the others, and smiled at its words (27:18-19).
76: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Quran?
From Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, including Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, ‘Isa… There were many other prophets not mentioned.
77: A young soldier in Talut's army, he killed Jalut. Allah then gave him kingship and wisdom (2:251).
78: Which book was revealed to Dawud?
Dawud had a magnificent voice: the mountains and the birds glorified Allah with him (34:10).
79: According to the Quran, ‘Isa came to confirm the Torah and to announce a messenger after him (61:6).
80: What is the name of ‘Isa's mother?
Daughter of ‘Imran, she was entrusted to Zakariyya and devoted to the worship of Allah. A whole surah bears her name.
81: Which prophet is called “Khalil Allah”, the close friend of Allah?
“And Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend” (4:125).
82: Which prophet is called “Kalim Allah”, the one to whom Allah spoke directly?
83: Which prophet was tested by a long illness and remained patient?
He lost his health, wealth and children without complaining to anyone but Allah, who gave everything back to him twice over (21:83-84).
84: Which prophet was sent to the people of ‘Ad?
A powerful people of builders, destroyed by an icy wind for 7 nights and 8 days (69:6-7).
85: Which prophet was sent to the people of Thamud, with a she-camel as a sign?
They killed the she-camel despite the warning, and a terrible blast destroyed them.
86: Which prophet was sent to the people of Madyan?
He called his people to stop cheating on measures and weights in trade.
87: Which prophet is the father of Yahya (John the Baptist)?
Very old, with a barren wife, he prayed to Allah, who gave him Yahya.
88: For which prophet did fire become coolness and peace?
“O fire, be coolness and peace for Ibrahim” (21:69), after he had broken his people's idols.
89: Which prophet interpreted the Egyptian king's dream of the seven fat cows?
He foretold 7 years of plenty followed by 7 of famine, which allowed Egypt to store reserves.
90: Which brother helped Musa in his mission?
Musa had asked Allah to give him his brother as a helper, because Harun spoke more eloquently (28:34).
91: Which prophet grew up in Pharaoh's palace?
His mother placed him in a chest on the Nile; he was taken in by Pharaoh's wife.
92: Which prophet is the son of Dawud?
He inherited prophethood and kingship from his father (27:16).
93: Which prophet is the father of Yusuf?
Also called Isra'il. He lost his sight from grief over Yusuf and regained it thanks to his shirt (12:93-96).
94: According to the Quran, for how many years did Nuh call his people?
95: What name does the Quran give to Ibrahim's father?
Ibrahim gently called him to give up the idols, without success (19:42-47).
96: Which prophet is called “Dhun-Nun”, the man of the fish?
“Nun” means fish in Arabic. The Quran also calls him “the companion of the fish” (68:48).
97: Which of these prophets is NOT one of the “Ulul-‘Azm” (the prophets of firm resolve)?
The five are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, ‘Isa and Muhammad ﷺ.
98: To which prophet, along with Musa, were “Scrolls” (Suhuf) revealed?
99: Which prophet is the son of Ibrahim and Sara?
The angels announced his birth to Sara, very old, who laughed in astonishment (11:71-72).
100: According to tradition, what is the name of Pharaoh's believing wife?
The Quran cites her as an example of faith against Pharaoh (66:11), and the Prophet ﷺ counted her among the perfect women (Bukhari).
101: To which prophet were the people of Sodom linked?
His people were destroyed for their evil deeds; his own wife was among the losers.
102: How many pillars of Islam are there?
The shahada, prayer, zakat, fasting in Ramadan and pilgrimage (hadith of Jibril, Muslim).
103: What is the first pillar of Islam?
“La ilaha illa Llah, Muhammadun rasulu Llah”: none deserves worship but Allah, and Muhammad is His messenger.
104: How many obligatory prayers are there each day?
Fajr, Dhuhr, ‘Asr, Maghrib and ‘Isha'. They were prescribed during the Mi‘raj.
105: What is the obligatory almsgiving called?
106: Which direction do Muslims face when they pray?
At first the prayer was towards Jerusalem. The qibla was turned to the Ka‘ba about 16 months after the Hijra (2:144).
107: What is the call to prayer called?
It was instituted in Medina after the dream of ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd; Bilal was chosen for his beautiful voice (Abu Dawud).
108: What is the purification done before prayer called?
Washing the face, the arms up to the elbows, wiping the head and washing the feet (5:6).
109: How many pillars of faith (arkan al-iman) are there?
Belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and destiny (hadith of Jibril, Muslim).
110: Which festival marks the end of Ramadan?
On the 1st of Shawwal. Fasting on that day is forbidden.
111: Which festival is also called “the festival of sacrifice”?
On the 10th of Dhul-Hijja. It commemorates the sacrifice of Ibrahim.
112: What is the dawn prayer called?
The 2 sunna rak‘as before Fajr are better than this world and all it contains (Muslim).
113: How many rak‘as does the Maghrib prayer have?
It is the only obligatory prayer of 3 rak‘as, and it is not shortened when travelling.
114: How many rak‘as does the Fajr prayer have?
The shortest, but one of the heaviest for the hypocrite, according to the hadith (Bukhari, Muslim).
115: How many rak‘as does the Dhuhr prayer have?
On Friday it is replaced by the Jumu‘a prayer: 2 rak‘as preceded by a sermon.
116: What is the circling around the Ka‘ba called?
It starts at the corner of the Black Stone, keeping the Ka‘ba on one's left.
117: How many circuits around the Ka‘ba are made during tawaf?
In the arrival tawaf, men walk briskly (ar-raml) during the first three circuits.
118: Between which hills do pilgrims walk back and forth (the sa‘y)?
In memory of Hajar, who ran between the two hills looking for water for Isma‘il, before Zamzam gushed out (Bukhari).
119: What is the most important day of Hajj, when pilgrims stand in supplication?
“Hajj is ‘Arafa” (Tirmidhi). It is the best day to call upon Allah.
120: What is the usual rate of zakat on money saved for a year?
That is one fortieth of money that reaches the threshold (nisab) and is held for a lunar year.
121: What is the meal eaten before dawn during Ramadan called?
Iftar is the meal that breaks the fast, at sunset.
122: What is the charity given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer called?
About 2.5 kg of staple food per person, so that the poor can celebrate Eid too.
123: What is the purification done without water, using clean earth, called?
When water is lacking or cannot be used, for example because of illness (5:6).
124: What is the pilgrim's state of consecration called?
Men wear two pieces of unstitched white cloth: everyone is equal before Allah.
125: Which of these is NOT one of the six pillars of faith?
The six: Allah, the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Day and destiny.
126: What is the blessed spring near the Ka‘ba called?
It gushed out for Hajar and Isma‘il. “The water of Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for” (Ibn Maja).
127: What is the lesser pilgrimage, possible all year round, called?
It includes ihram, tawaf and sa‘y, then shaving or cutting the hair.
128: What are the extra night prayers during Ramadan called?
The Prophet ﷺ prayed them in congregation for a few nights, then stopped for fear they would become obligatory (Bukhari).
129: In which month of the Hijri calendar does Hajj take place?
The 12th and last month. Its first ten days are the best days of the year (Bukhari).
130: What is the spiritual retreat in the mosque during the last ten days of Ramadan called?
The Prophet ﷺ did it every year during the last ten days of Ramadan (Bukhari, Muslim).
131: Which prayer is performed standing, without bowing or prostrating?
It has 4 takbirs. Attending until the burial brings two great rewards, “as large as two mountains” (Bukhari, Muslim).
132: What is the minimum amount of wealth on which zakat is due called?
Hawl is the lunar year during which the wealth must be held.
133: Where do pilgrims spend the night after ‘Arafa?
Pilgrims often collect the pebbles there for the stoning at Mina.
134: How many small pebbles are thrown at the pillar of ‘Aqaba on the day of sacrifice?
On the following days, 7 pebbles are thrown at each of the three pillars of Mina.
135: Who was the first caliph after the Prophet ﷺ?
He ruled for just over two years (632-634) and had the Quran compiled.
136: A 10-year caliphate (634-644), during which Islam spread to Persia, Syria and Egypt.
137: A 12-year caliphate (644-656). He was killed in his home while reading the Quran.
138: Caliph from 656 to 661. He was the first child to believe in the Prophet ﷺ.
139: In which year of the common era did the Hijra take place?
It is year 1 of the Hijri calendar, chosen later by ‘Umar.
140: What are the first four caliphs called?
“Hold fast to my sunna and that of the rightly guided caliphs” (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi).
141: Which city is the third holy city of Islam?
It was the first qibla and the destination of the night journey.
142: Which famous mosque is in Jerusalem?
“The farthest mosque” (17:1), destination of the Prophet's ﷺ night journey.
143: Which caliph introduced the Hijri calendar?
Around 638, he chose the Hijra as the starting point, on ‘Ali's suggestion.
144: Under which caliph did Jerusalem come under Muslim rule?
Around 638, ‘Umar came in person to receive the city and guaranteed the safety of its people.
145: Which dynasty succeeded the Rightly Guided Caliphs?
Founded by Mu‘awiya in 661, the dynasty ruled until 750.
146: What was the capital of the Umayyads?
The Great Umayyad Mosque was built there under the caliph al-Walid I.
147: Which city did the Abbasids found as their capital?
Founded in 762 by the caliph al-Mansur in the shape of a circle: it was called “the Round City”.
148: What was the great centre of learning and translation in Baghdad called?
Scholars there translated Greek, Persian and Indian books of science and philosophy into Arabic.
149: Which Muslim leader took back Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187?
He spared the inhabitants, unlike the massacre committed by the Crusaders in 1099.
150: The Muslim presence there lasted from 711 to 1492, nearly eight centuries.
151: Which city of Al-Andalus is famous for its great mosque?
Capital of the Umayyad caliphate of Spain, it was one of the largest cities in Europe in the 10th century.
152: Which Muslim empire conquered Constantinople in 1453?
The city took the name Istanbul and remained the empire's capital until 1922.
153: Which Muslim scholar gave his name to the “algorithm” and is a father of algebra?
The word “algebra” comes from the title of his book: “al-jabr”.
154: Which physician wrote the famous “Canon of Medicine”?
His Canon was taught in European universities for several centuries.
155: Which Moroccan traveller journeyed across much of the world in the 14th century?
Setting out from Tangier in 1325, he travelled for nearly 30 years, as far as China.
156: Which thinker wrote the “Muqaddima”, often seen as a founding text of sociology?
Born in Tunis in 1332, he analyses in it the rise and fall of civilisations.
157: Which general crossed the strait to Spain in 711?
The name “Gibraltar” comes from “Jabal Tariq”, Tariq's mountain.
158: Which university in Fez, founded by a woman, Fatima al-Fihriyya, is one of the oldest in the world still operating?
Founded in 859 thanks to Fatima al-Fihriyya's inheritance.
159: Which famous palace is in Granada?
Palace of the Nasrids, the last Muslim dynasty of Spain, famous for its gardens and arabesques.
160: In which year did Granada, the last kingdom of Al-Andalus, fall?
King Boabdil handed the city over to the Catholic Monarchs, the same year as Columbus's voyage.
161: Which city was founded by the Fatimids in 969?
They also founded the al-Azhar mosque there, which later became a great Sunni university.
162: Which scholar is considered the father of modern optics?
He showed that sight comes from light entering the eye, not from rays coming out of it.
163: He was 21. A hadith foretelling this conquest is often quoted, but its authenticity is debated.
164: In which year was Baghdad destroyed by the Mongols?
The Mongols killed the Abbasid caliph and threw so many books into the Tigris that the water, it is said, turned black with ink.
165: The word comes from the same root as “salam”, peace.
166: What is the first month of the Hijri calendar?
It is one of the four sacred months. Fasting on the day of ‘Ashura', the 10th, is recommended.
167: “Alhamdulillah” fills the scale of good deeds (Muslim).
168: It is said when speaking about a future action (18:23-24).
169: What is the whole of the Prophet's ﷺ sayings, actions and approvals called?
With the Quran, it is the second source of Islam.
170: Which companion was the first muezzin of Islam?
A former slave tortured for his faith, he kept repeating “Ahad, Ahad” (One, One). Abu Bakr bought him to set him free.
171: Which companion is called “As-Siddiq”, the truthful?
He immediately believed the account of the night journey when others doubted: “If he said it, then it is true.”
172: Which companion is called “Al-Faruq”, the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood?
His conversion gave strength to the Muslims, who could then pray openly near the Ka‘ba.
173: How many months are there in the Hijri calendar?
“The number of months with Allah is twelve” (9:36).
174: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ cousin and son-in-law?
Son of Abu Talib, he married Fatima, the Prophet's ﷺ daughter.
175: Which caliph is called “Dhun-Nurayn” because he married two of the Prophet's ﷺ daughters?
He married Ruqayya and then, after her death, Umm Kulthum.
176: Which companion narrated the largest number of hadiths?
More than 5,000 hadiths. His nickname means “the father of the kitten”.
177: Which wife of the Prophet ﷺ is famous for her great knowledge and narrated many hadiths?
Daughter of Abu Bakr, she narrated more than 2,000 hadiths, and the great companions came to consult her.
178: Which companion is called “the Sword of Allah”?
The Prophet ﷺ gave him this nickname at the battle of Mu'ta (Bukhari).
179: Bilal came from Abyssinia, and Suhayb had grown up among the Byzantines (Rum).
180: Which two hadith collections are considered the most authentic?
The Sunan of Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi
Al-Bukhari chose his hadiths from among hundreds of thousands, with very strict conditions.
181: Who was the first woman martyr of Islam?
Mother of ‘Ammar ibn Yasir, she was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to renounce her faith.
182: What is Ramadan's position in the Hijri calendar?
Fasting this month is one of the five pillars of Islam.
183: Those who emigrated to Medina are called the Muhajirun, and those who welcomed them the Ansar.
184: The day Allah saved Musa from Pharaoh. The Prophet ﷺ fasted it and wanted to add the 9th (Muslim).
185: Which of these scholars did NOT found a Sunni school of law?
The four schools: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi‘i and Hanbali.
186: Which school of law is the majority in Morocco?
As in the whole Maghreb and much of West Africa. It is named after Imam Malik of Medina.
187: How many companions were promised Paradise in a single hadith?
Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthman, ‘Ali, Talha, az-Zubayr, ‘Abd ar-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa‘id ibn Zayd and Abu ‘Ubayda (Tirmidhi).
188: Which wife of the Prophet ﷺ was ‘Umar's daughter?
The Quran compiled under Abu Bakr was kept at her home.
189: Which companion was called “the trustworthy one of this community”?
Reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim. He is one of the ten promised Paradise.
190: Which young companion did the Prophet ﷺ appoint to lead an army just before his death?
He was about 18. After the Prophet's ﷺ death, Abu Bakr still sent the army as planned.
191: What title do the Prophet's ﷺ wives hold?
“His wives are their mothers” (33:6), as a sign of respect.
192: Which school of law is the majority in Turkey?
It was the official school of the Ottoman Empire. It is named after Imam Abu Hanifa.
193: Which imam wrote the “Muwatta'”, one of the oldest hadith collections?
“The smoothed path”. Imam Malik lived in Medina, the city of the Prophet ﷺ.
194: You sneeze. What do you say?
The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah loves sneezing and dislikes yawning (Bukhari).
195: Someone sneezes and says “Alhamdulillah”. What do you reply?
“Yarhamuka Llah” (may Allah have mercy on you)
They then reply: “Yahdikumu Llah wa yuslihu balakum” (may Allah guide you and set your affairs right).
196: Someone says “As-salamu ‘alaykum” to you. What do you reply?
Answering the salam is obligatory; giving it first is recommended.
197: What do you say before you start eating?
The Prophet ﷺ told a child: “Say Bismillah, eat with your right hand and from what is in front of you” (Bukhari, Muslim).
198: With which hand did the Prophet ﷺ recommend eating and drinking?
According to the hadith, Satan eats and drinks with his left hand (Muslim).
199: What do you say when you have finished eating?
Allah is pleased with the servant who praises Him after eating or drinking (Muslim).
200: You talk about what you will do tomorrow. Which phrase do you add?
The Quran asks for it in Surah Al-Kahf (18:23-24).
201: You hear that someone has died. What do you say?
“We belong to Allah and to Him we return” (2:156).
202: You made a mistake or committed a sin. Which phrase do you say to ask Allah's forgiveness?
The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah's forgiveness more than 70 times a day (Bukhari).
203: You find a friend's baby beautiful. What do you say?
We call for blessing (baraka) on what pleases us.
204: According to a hadith, smiling at your brother is…
205: What do we say before starting to read the Quran?
We seek Allah's protection from Satan (16:98).
206: A stone or dangerous object is lying in the middle of the path. What do you do?
I remove it so that nobody gets hurt
I walk around it, it's not my problem
I leave it, someone else will do it
I show it to my friends and carry on
According to a hadith, removing something harmful from the path is a branch of faith.
207: With which foot do we enter the mosque, according to the sunna?
We leave with the left foot. On entering we say: “Allahumma ftah li abwaba rahmatik” (Muslim).
208: Your friend tells you a secret. What do you do?
I keep it: it is a trust (amana)
I share it if it's funny
Betraying what is entrusted to us is one of the signs of a hypocrite (Bukhari, Muslim).
209: Your parents ask you for something that annoys you. How do you behave?
I speak to them gently and respectfully
I raise my voice so they understand
The Quran asks us to be good to our parents and to speak to them respectfully (17:23).
210: What do we say when entering our home?
If one mentions Allah when entering, Satan tells his companions: “No night's stay or dinner here for you” (Muslim).
211: You promised someone something. What must you do?
Forget it if it's a small promise
Keep it only if it's written
Keep it only if they are Muslim
“And fulfil the covenant, for every covenant will be questioned” (17:34).
212: You yawn. What does the sunna recommend?
Holding it back and putting your hand over your mouth
Yawning comes from Satan; hold it back as much as you can (Bukhari, Muslim).
213: Your neighbour, who is not Muslim, needs help. What does Islam teach you?
Help them: a neighbour has rights, whoever they are
Help only if they are Muslim
Wait until they ask three times
The Prophet ﷺ said that Jibril kept urging him to care for the neighbour.
214: You are very angry. What did the Prophet ﷺ advise?
Seek refuge in Allah from Satan and sit down if you are standing
A man asked for advice. The Prophet ﷺ answered: “Do not get angry”, and repeated it several times (Bukhari).
215: Someone asks you for help but you have nothing to give. What do you do?
I answer kindly: a good word is charity
216: How should a Muslim treat animals?
Gently: kindness to them is rewarded
However he likes, they're just animals
He must not go near them
According to a hadith, a man was forgiven for giving water to a thirsty dog.
217: A friend is ill. What does visiting them mean?
Whoever visits a sick person remains in the gardens of Paradise until he returns (Muslim).
218: Someone did you a favour. Which phrase do we say to thank them?
219: According to the hadith, who most deserves your good companionship?
The Prophet ﷺ answered “your mother” three times, then “your father”.
220: A classmate makes a mistake and the others mock him. What do you do?
I don't mock him and I stand up for him
I mock him too to fit in
I film it for a laugh
221: During Ramadan, you ate by mistake. What do you do?
I continue my fast until sunset
I stop fasting for the day
I give charity instead of fasting

222: You forgot to say “Bismillah” at the start of the meal. What do you say when you remember?
Reported by Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi.
223: According to the Quran (4:86), how should a greeting be answered?
With an equal or better greeting
Only if you know the person
To “As-salamu ‘alaykum” one can reply “Wa ‘alaykumu s-salam wa rahmatu Llah”.
224: Saying something true about an absent person that they would not like to hear
If what is said is false, it is even worse: it is slander (buhtan).
225: In the Quran, what is backbiting compared to?
Eating the flesh of one's dead brother
226: Someone carries tales to set two people against each other. What is this sin called?
“The tale-bearer will not enter Paradise” (Bukhari, Muslim).
227: You receive a serious rumour about someone in a WhatsApp group. What does the Quran ask?
Verify the information before believing or sharing it
Believe it if several people repeat it
228: You have fallen out with a Muslim friend. For how many days at most did the Prophet ﷺ allow giving each other the cold shoulder?
“It is not permitted for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three days” (Bukhari, Muslim).

The one waiting for an apology

Stay kind to them, without obeying them in what goes against faith
Only talk to them about religion

Repel evil with what is better

233: You are travelling. What concession is allowed for the 4-rak‘a prayers?
Maghrib (3 rak‘as) and Fajr (2 rak‘as) are not shortened.
234: You overslept and missed the Fajr prayer. What do you do?
I pray it as soon as I wake up
I pray it the next day with the other Fajr
“Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, let him pray it as soon as he remembers it” (Muslim).
235: With which foot do scholars recommend entering the toilet?
The right is kept for what is noble (the mosque, putting on shoes…), the left for the opposite. On entering one says: “Allahumma inni a‘udhu bika mina l-khubuthi wa l-khaba'ith” (Bukhari, Muslim).
236: Someone gives you a gift. What did the Prophet ﷺ do?
He accepted gifts and gave in return
He gave them straight to someone else
“Give gifts to one another and you will love one another” (Bukhari, al-Adab al-Mufrad).
237: You are invited to a friend's wedding meal (walima). What does the sunna recommend?
Declining so as not to be a bother
“If one of you is invited to a wedding meal, let him attend” (Bukhari, Muslim).
238: “None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother…”

… as much as he loves his parents
Reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Anas.

No, we only swear by Allah
Yes, if it's to tell the truth
Yes, but only for small things
“Whoever swears, let him swear by Allah or remain silent” (Bukhari, Muslim).

He lies, betrays trust and breaks his promises

Nothing, you sit down straight away

244: What must you avoid when someone is praying?
Walking right in front of them
Reading the Quran in the same room
If he knew how serious it is, he would rather wait forty than pass in front (Bukhari, Muslim).

Eat and drink, but do not waste
Eat as much as you like
The Prophet ﷺ advised a third for food, a third for drink and a third for air in the stomach (Tirmidhi).

… does not live near a mosque
249: According to the hadith, the true Muslim is the one from whom others are safe…
… from his tongue and his hand
250: According to a hadith, why did a woman enter Hell?
She locked up a cat without feeding it
She neither fed it nor let it look for food itself (Bukhari, Muslim).
251: According to the hadith, “the best of you is…”
… the one who has travelled most
“… and I am the best of you to my family” (Tirmidhi).
252: During prayer you are unsure: 3 or 4 rak‘as? What do you do?
I count 3, complete the prayer and do the prostrations of forgetfulness (sujud as-sahw)
I start the prayer again from the beginning
You rely on what is certain, that is, the smaller number.
253: You get into a car or a plane. Which supplication does the Quran teach?
“Glory be to the One who has placed this at our service” (43:13).
254: You swore by Allah to do something, then did not do it. What is the expiation (kaffara)?
Feed or clothe ten poor people, otherwise fast three days
Give one euro to the mosque
255: In which cases did the Prophet ﷺ tolerate not telling the exact truth?
To reconcile people, in war, and between spouses to get along
Hadith of Umm Kulthum (Muslim). Deceiving to cause harm remains forbidden.
256: You find a lost wallet in the street. What does the sunna say?
Announce it to find its owner
Keep it, it's a gift from Allah
Give the money to the poor straight away
The hadith asks that a found item be made known for a year.
257: What do we say when leaving home, according to the sunna?
“Bismillah, tawakkaltu ‘ala Llah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah”
It is then said to him: “You are guided, protected and kept safe” (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi).
258: According to the Quran (25:63), how do the servants of the Most Merciful answer when the ignorant provoke them?
It is the start of the portrait of “the servants of the Most Merciful”, at the end of Surah Al-Furqan.
259: According to the hadith, what does the sunna recommend before the Friday prayer?
Bathing (ghusl), wearing perfume and good clothes
Arriving just at the end of the sermon
Reported by al-Bukhari. Using the siwak is also recommended.
260: You see an injustice. According to the hadith, what is the weakest degree of faith?
The hadith says: change it with your hand, otherwise with your tongue, otherwise with your heart.
261: The Prophet ﷺ advised Abu Dharr, when he makes a broth…
… to add water and give some to his neighbours
… to keep it for the next day
Reported by Muslim. Neighbours have great rights in Islam.
262: Which surah is recited in every rak‘a of the prayer?
“There is no prayer for whoever does not recite the Fatiha” (Bukhari, Muslim).

268: What does “Al-Baqara”, the name of the 2nd surah, mean?
It tells the story of the cow the Children of Israel had to sacrifice (2:67-73).
269: What does “Al-Fil”, the name of Surah 105, mean?
It tells of Abraha's army coming to destroy the Ka‘ba, the year the Prophet ﷺ was born.
270: Which surah is named after a fruit?
It begins with “By the fig and the olive”.
271: How many verses does the Quran have, according to the most widespread count?
The often-quoted figure of 6,666 is not accurate.

May Allah's blessings and peace be upon him
May Allah be pleased with him

275: Could the Prophet ﷺ read and write?

276: What work did the Prophet ﷺ do for Khadija?
Khadija was impressed by his honesty, then proposed marriage to him.
277: In which battle did archers leave their post, causing heavy losses?
In the year 3 AH. Thinking the battle won, the archers left the hill despite the Prophet's ﷺ order.
278: On which day of the week was the Prophet ﷺ born?
He also received the first revelation on a Monday.
279: According to the Quran, he was neither killed nor crucified, but raised up to Allah (4:157-158).
280: Which prophet parted the sea with his staff?
Pharaoh and his army drowned while chasing him (26:63-66).
281: Which prophet was ordered to sacrifice his son, who was then replaced by a ram?
Ibrahim and his son accepted Allah's command: this is the origin of the Eid al-Adha sacrifice (37:102-107).
282: Who is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran?
No other woman, not even the Prophet's ﷺ wives, is called by name in the Quran.
283: According to the hadith, what was the name of the young servant who accompanied Musa in search of al-Khidr?
He later led the Children of Israel to the Holy Land.
284: What is the month of fasting called?
It is the 9th month of the Hijri calendar.
285: One abstains from eating, drinking and marital relations (2:187).
286: What is the meal that breaks the fast called?
People will remain in good as long as they hasten to break the fast (Bukhari, Muslim).
287: On which day is the great weekly congregational prayer?
“O you who believe, when the call is made for the Friday prayer, hasten to the remembrance of Allah” (62:9).
288: What is the person who makes the call to prayer called?
According to the hadith, muezzins will have the longest necks on the Day of Resurrection, a sign of honour (Muslim).
289: What is the sunset prayer called?
It is prayed just after sunset, when the fast is broken in Ramadan.
290: What do we say to begin the prayer?
This first takbir is called “takbirat al-ihram”: it brings you into the prayer.
291: How many times in a lifetime is the pilgrimage (Hajj) obligatory?
Once, for those who are able

292: How many rak‘as does the ‘Isha' prayer have?
It is the last obligatory prayer of the day, after nightfall.
293: How many rak‘as does the ‘Asr prayer have?
For many scholars, it is “the middle prayer” that must be especially guarded (2:238).
294: What do we say in prostration (sujud)?
In bowing (ruku‘) we say “Subhana rabbiya l-‘azim”.
295: During the Mi‘raj, how many prayers were first prescribed before being reduced to 5?
On Musa's advice, the Prophet ﷺ asked for a reduction. The 5 prayers carry the reward of 50 (Bukhari, Muslim).
296: What is the holiest city in Islam?
It is home to the Ka‘ba and the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram).
297: What is the second holy city of Islam?
The Prophet ﷺ lived his last ten years there and is buried there.
298: From which event does the Muslim calendar start?
The Hijra, the emigration to Medina
It starts in 622, year 1 of the Hijra.
299: The Muslim calendar is based on…
Months begin with the new crescent. The lunar year has about 354 days, 11 fewer than the solar year.
300: Which city did the Ottomans choose as their capital after 1453?
Hagia Sophia was then turned into a mosque.
301: Which Umayyad caliph had the Dome of the Rock built in Jerusalem?
Completed around 691. It stands on the al-Aqsa esplanade, but it is not the al-Aqsa mosque itself.

A great-grandson of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab through his mother, he ruled briefly (717-720) but with great justice.

311: According to the hadith, how many names of Allah open Paradise to whoever learns them?
Allah has other names He keeps in His knowledge: the hadith does not limit them to 99.
312: It comes from “rahma”, mercy. Ar-Rahim, the Especially Merciful, is close to it.

With the supplication “Bismika Llahumma amutu wa ahya” (Bukhari).

Repeat the words of the muezzin

319: How did the Prophet ﷺ drink?
In three sips, breathing outside the cup
Blowing into the glass to cool it
He forbade blowing or breathing into the vessel (Bukhari, Muslim).
320: Which supplication do we say when entering the mosque?
On leaving, we say “Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik” (Muslim).
321: After each prayer, what do we say 33 times each, according to the sunna?
The hundred is completed with “La ilaha illa Llahu wahdahu la sharika lah…” (Muslim).
322: According to the hadith, what is the best remembrance of Allah (dhikr)?
“The best dhikr is la ilaha illa Llah, and the best supplication is alhamdulillah” (Tirmidhi).
323: How did the Prophet ﷺ eat?
With three fingers of his right hand, then he licked his fingers
Very fast, without talking to anyone
He said: “You do not know in which part of your food the blessing lies” (Muslim).

Seek Allah's protection and tell no one about it
Write it down to have it interpreted
Stay awake the rest of the night

“As if he had fasted the whole year” (Muslim).

He helped his family with the household chores
He only came home to sleep
‘A'isha: he mended his clothes, repaired his sandals and served his family (Bukhari, Ahmad).
334: How did the Prophet ﷺ behave with children?
